answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a small stake on a public ledge: anyone may inspect it, and an attacker spawning a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred ledges, so the cost of fakery scales linearly while honest participation costs once. Past behaviour is then recorded in an atlas of attestations — each verified trade or honest vote adds a stamped entry strangers can read before trusting a newcomer. An identity slashed for fraud becomes a relic of the ledger: visible, unusable, a warning that reputation is earned slowly and lost in a single act.
